main_text.p: Dei erga creaturam corruptam atq; peccatricem declaratio, quæ refipiscentibus veniam peccatorum nono fferat[?]. Idcirco id affirmauit Amyraldus, & consentaneum esse putauit cum doctrina Calvini, Comm. in Ezechielem, cap. 18. v. 23. An cupio mortem impij &c. Confirmat eandem sententiam, aliys verbis, Deum scilicet nihil magis cupere, quàm ut quicunque peribant, & ruebant in mortem, redeant in viam salutis. Et hac etiam de causa non modo hodie Euangelium promulgatur in mundo, sed omnibus saeculis voluit Deus testatum esse quàm propensus sit ad misericordiam. Nam Profani quam-vis lege & prophetis carerent, tamen semper gustu aliquo huius doctrina fuerunt praditi. Verum quidem est suffocatam fuisse mul-tis erroribus ; sed reperiemus semper arca-no impulsu fuisse adductos ad petendam veniam, quia hic sensus quodammodo in-genitus illis erat, Deum esse omnibus qui ipsum quaerunt placabilem. Caterum, clarius id Deus in lege & Prophetis testatus est. In Euangelio autem scimus quàm familiariter nos compellet, vbi promittit no-bis veniam. Neque verò aliter Ethnici de Dei natura existimarunt.

page.notes: The first line is set as running text, not as a running head. The page ends mid-sentence at the foot of the scan. The word "fferat" is marked [?] because the start of the word is unclear. The text is set in bold; italic passages are marked. Printed "vt" and "Calui-" are given as "ut" and "Calvi-" under the spelling rule for u/v. Per the instructions, the printed forms are left as they are. The first line is a fragment, continuing from the part of the page above the cut. Some words are set in roman and some in italic, and the boundaries in "Deus in lege" and "Prophetis" were hard to tell apart. The initial "de" in the last line has a decorative flourish. The "E" of "Ethnici" is partly damaged but reads as printed. Spelling is as printed, with long s written as s and u/v normalised.
